selection_rules: Choose the layout from the message type, not from how decorative it looks.
Use one conclusion per slide and place that conclusion in the title.
Use medium density for normal body slides; reserve sparse layouts for deliberate covers, dividers, quotes, and pauses.
Never shrink body text to rescue an overloaded layout; split the slide instead.
Use a cover once, a divider only at a real chapter boundary, and a closing once.

In a light system, keep no more than two dark slides in succession unless the section is intentionally dramatic; a deliberate research-operating-system archetype may remain dark throughout when projector contrast and chapter pauses pass QA.
If brand colors are absent, select exactly one theme from the audience and scenario; do not ask a beginner to compare palettes.

style_archetypes.clear_defense: White canvas, restrained institutional color, persistent chapter navigation, titled evidence zones, and explicit interpretation bands.
style_archetypes.consulting_nerdy: Dense analytical canvas with claim headlines, spatial zones, direct annotations, and one decision implication.
style_archetypes.institutional_research: Stable logo safe area, consistent header or section rail, neutral evidence canvas, and disciplined brand color.
style_archetypes.scientific_editorial: Editorial scientific cover, pale evidence pages, numbered sections, schematic diagrams, direct finding statements, and source lines.
style_archetypes.research_operating_system: Deep navy canvas, cyan structural lines, semantic accent colors, numbered modules, stable interface-like frames, and sparse chapter pauses.
style_archetypes.figure_first_paper_review: White evidence canvas, oxblood accent, fixed title rule and slide number, dominant scientific figures, and repeated question-evidence-summary loops.
